title: Velvet Hour monthly gig package: cut a sizzle reel + vertical reframe from last month's long single-camera set take, match four mismatched-light artist promos to one grey-card white point, give them the venue's signature single-hue duotone poster treatment, vectorize the venue mark, and data-merge a four-page lineup listing

source.reference: Live Music Session Editor & Monthly Promo Designer

grounding_note: Adapted from a real Upwork brief for a recurring live-music editor/promo designer (a small venue that films one session a month for its social channels and needs both a short social edit and printed promo for the next lineup, house style 'clean, coherent, story-first, no gimmicks', distribution across Instagram/Facebook/YouTube). The real post named no brand; the venue is laundered to the fictional 'Velvet Hour' monthly live-music night (a moth-and-lamp mark), and the four upcoming performers are fictional ('Junie Ash', 'The Paper Kestrels', 'Odette Vann', 'Cinder & Salt'). REPOSITIONED for connector reality: the KILLED version tried to sell a footage-REVIEW findings log (workflow_nature analyze, three locally-authored report PDFs, asset_preview_file standing in for a real frame pull) and produced no designed artifact. This rebuild honours the connector's actual video reality (video contributes an AI-picked cut via video_create_quick_cut, a same-length reframe via video_resize, and frame pulls via video_render_frame — no timeline trims, no motion graphics, no compositing) and puts the OWNED designed work where the tools can actually do it: an agent-authored matched-and-duotoned promo image set, a prep-before-trace vector venue mark, and a one-record-per-page InDesign data-merge lineup listing. Everything typeset comes from the InDesign lane; the video lane only cuts, reframes and pulls stills. No real person, brand, product or trademark is named anywhere.
one_line_ask: Cut a short social sizzle reel and a vertical story reframe from last month's long single-camera Velvet Hour set take, pull a poster still from the footage; then take four promo photos of next month's four artists (shot by different people under mismatched light, each with a grey reference card in frame), neutralise each to its card so the set reads as one white point, give the set the venue's signature single-hue duotone poster treatment matched to one density, vectorize the scanned venue mark, and data-merge the authored InDesign listing template so every artist gets one printed lineup page.
full_brief:
Velvet Hour is a monthly intimate live-music night. Every month we film one acoustic set in one long, continuous single-camera take for our socials (Instagram, Facebook, YouTube) and we print a one-page-per-artist lineup sheet for the door and for the next month's promo. We are NOT reshooting anything and we do NOT want a fancy motion-graphics edit — our house style is clean, coherent, performance-first, no gimmicks. Here is the whole job, in three parts.

PART 1 - the social cut. From last month's raw footage - one long, continuous, several-minutes-long single-camera take that runs the whole stripped-back set on a locked wide of the little stage - give us one short, punchy social sizzle reel that captures the feel of the night, plus a vertical 9:16 version of that same reel for stories. Same length is fine for the vertical - just reframed so the performer stays in shot. Also pull one strong still frame out of the footage that we can treat as a gig-night poster image (see the look in Part 2).

PART 2 - the artist promos, matched then treated. Next month's lineup is four acts and their promo photos were sent in by four different people, shot on different days under whatever light they had, so straight out of the folder they read like four separate shoots. Every photographer left a standard 18% grey reference card at the edge of the frame. First, bring all four to one consistent look: neutralise each photo to the grey card it carries so that card reads truly neutral and the four sit at one shared white point and brightness - a viewer scrolling the lineup should not be able to tell they were shot by four different people on four different days. Judge every frame on its own in-frame grey card and land it on that shared target; then TELL US the white-balance and exposure move you settled on for each one so we can see the set was matched, not eyeballed. Hand back BOTH the neutralised full frames with the grey card still in shot (keep those as our proof-of-match masters so we can confirm each card really reads neutral and the four match) AND the same frames cropped to web thumbnails with the card removed. Then, on top of the matched set, give the four our signature Velvet Hour poster look: a single-hue duotone (a deep tonal treatment in one house colour, dark and moody but never crushed to dead black, punchy contrast, all four sitting at ONE matched density so the printed lineup reads as one series). The poster look has to be built as a deliberate tonal grade, not a one-click filter, and all four have to land at one shared density. Give us the four duotone posters too.

PART 3 - the mark and the printed listing. Our venue mark only exists as a flat scan on off-white paper, a little crooked, with a margin around it - clean it up and vectorise it razor-sharp for the listing masthead: straighten it, knock the paper ground off the OUTSIDE of the lettering, and set it into the pale masthead of the listing sheet (that is the only place it needs to go on this job). Finally, build the lineup sheet: we have hand-built the InDesign listing template with the real placeholder fields and two image slots (one for the artist's poster, one in the masthead for our venue mark), and we are sending the lineup data file; merge them so every artist gets their own single page with their duotone poster placed, our venue mark in the masthead, and their name, genre, set date, set time and one-line blurb set in type, and hand back a press-ready PDF - one page per artist, four artists, four pages. Bind our copy verbatim from the data file; do not rewrite it. Acceptance: every grey card neutral and the four matched to one white point (with your per-photo moves reported); the four duotone posters at one shared density (deep but nothing clipped to pure black); the mark a clean, skew-free vector with the paper knocked off the OUTSIDE of the lettering, sitting cleanly in the pale listing masthead; and exactly one finished listing page per lineup row.

inputs.name: velvet_hour_lastmonth_set_take
inputs.gen_prompt: A single, long, continuous, ungraded 4K (3840x2160) locked-off camera take of a fictional singer-songwriter playing a stripped-back acoustic set in a small dim warm-lit music room - one real camera on a tripod, framed as a locked wide of the little stage, rolling unbroken for the whole several-minutes-long performance (a real multi-minute capture, NOT a short clip). Native camera audio (guitar, vocals, faint warm room ambience, a little between-song murmur). Clean, well-exposed, steady, performance-focused footage with a warm amber stage-light feel. Flat camera-original look, no on-screen text or graphics, no music bed added, no colour grade baked in, no cuts - one uninterrupted take.
inputs.realism_notes: A REAL camera capture (not AI-generated): one long single-camera take, several minutes long, so it is genuinely longer than any cut made from it. The source for the video lane only: video_create_quick_cut SHORTENS this one long take to the sizzle reel (output duration < source; the creative cut is the tool's, not the agent's), video_resize makes the same-length 9:16 reframe of that shorter sizzle, and video_render_frame pulls one 4K still that the agent treats into the gig-night poster. Declared at 4K so both the 9:16 vertical crop still holds >=1080 width and a pulled frame downscales cleanly to a print-scale poster (never upscaled). Native audio so the quick-cut has real content to cut against. ONE camera, ONE unbroken take - no multi-camera intercut, no assembly of clips, no timeline trim, no motion graphics, no compositing is claimed anywhere - the connector cannot do them, and quick_cut can only shorten a single source that is longer than the cut.

inputs.name: promo_junie_ash.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal press/promo portrait of a fictional indie-folk singer 'Junie Ash', a young woman with an acoustic guitar seated by a large window, natural documentary feel, raw un-graded look. Shot under COOL overcast window light with a distinct blue-cyan cast and a slightly flat, marginally under-exposed exposure, and the whole frame sits a few degrees crooked (~3 deg tilt). A standard 18% neutral grey reference card and a small white swatch rest at the lower-LEFT edge of the frame. Real skin texture, hair detail, fabric weave; roughly 4000 px on the long edge, camera-original, not CGI-glossy.
inputs.realism_notes: Artist 1, Session A (cool/blue), tilted so image_auto_straighten has real work. Its grey card is the neutralisation target; the correct move is to WARM and lift toward the shared white point. ~4000 px so the 300 DPI listing page never needs upscaling. Grey card sits far-left so the listing crop removes it.

inputs.name: promo_paper_kestrels.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal press/promo portrait of a fictional alt-country duo 'The Paper Kestrels', two musicians with a guitar and a mandolin standing in a rehearsal room, natural documentary feel, raw un-graded look. Shot under WARM tungsten work-light with a strong orange cast and a slightly BRIGHT exposure. A standard 18% neutral grey reference card and a small white swatch rest at the lower-RIGHT edge of the frame. Real skin, denim and instrument-wood texture; roughly 4000 px on the long edge, camera-original, not CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: Artist 2, Session B (warm/orange, bright). Opposite correction sign to Junie: COOL the temperature and pull exposure DOWN to land its grey card neutral at the shared white point. Two frames, opposite moves - a uniform batch correction cannot fix both.

inputs.name: promo_odette_vann.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal press/promo portrait of a fictional jazz vocalist 'Odette Vann', a woman in a warm amber satin dress in front of a golden-brown draped backdrop holding a vintage microphone, natural documentary feel, raw un-graded look. Shot under clean NEUTRAL studio light (no colour cast, correct exposure) so the warmth in frame is the real styling and set, NOT a white-balance error - her in-frame 18% grey reference card and small white swatch, resting at the edge of the frame, ALREADY read neutral. Real satin sheen, skin and hair texture; roughly 4000 px on the long edge, camera-original, not CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: Artist 3 - THE TRAP. Shot under neutral light with an already-neutral grey card; the amber dress and golden backdrop are intentional styling. The correct move is essentially NO white-balance shift (only match exposure/density to the set). A naive agent that batch-applies a 'cool the warm frames' correction, or 'cools an imagined orange cast', neutralises the card off-neutral and strips the warm look she is selling. The decision must be driven by THIS card, not the batch.

inputs.name: promo_cinder_and_salt.jpg
inputs.gen_prompt: Photoreal press/promo portrait of a fictional post-punk trio 'Cinder & Salt', three musicians in dark clothing against a dark brick wall, moody, natural documentary feel, raw un-graded look. Shot under COOL overcast light with a blue cast and clearly UNDER-EXPOSED so the dark clothing and wall muddy toward black. A standard 18% neutral grey reference card and a small white swatch rest at the edge of the frame. Real fabric nap, skin and brick texture still readable in the shadows; roughly 4000 px on the long edge, camera-original, not CGI.
inputs.realism_notes: Artist 4, Session A (cool), dark and under-exposed. Warm to neutralise its grey card AND LIFT exposure to the set brightness while holding the black point - charcoal must stay charcoal, not crush to 0 or wash to grey. A different dominant move (tonal recovery) from the other three, and the frame most likely to lose shadow detail in the later duotone if its density is not matched first.

inputs.name: velvet_hour_mark_scan.png
inputs.gen_prompt: A flat desktop scan of the 'Velvet Hour' venue mark inked on off-white textured paper: a warm hand-lettered condensed serif wordmark with a small simple moth-over-a-lamp glyph, deep ink-black letters. Rendered as a real scan - the paper is a slightly warm off-white (NOT transparent, NOT pure white), the whole mark sits very slightly rotated (~2 deg) on the scan bed, there is extra paper margin around it, and the edges are a touch soft as a real scan would be. High enough contrast that, once cleaned, it will vectorize cleanly.
inputs.realism_notes: Scanned-on-paper (off-white ground, slight rotation, margin, soft edges) so image_vectorize would trace the paper and the skew if fed raw - forcing genuine prep-before-trace: straighten, boost contrast/clarity, crop to the mark, knock the OUTER off-white ground to transparency, THEN vectorize. The serif wordmark carries enclosed counters (the bowls of the three e's and the o in 'Velvet Hour'); image_remove_background isolates only the OUTER ground and cannot punch open an enclosed interior counter (ground-truth: enclosed negative space stays filled), so those counters crisp to WHITE, not transparent. That is why the mark is set only on the LIGHT listing masthead, where white-filled counters are invisible against the pale ground - the deliverable gates the trace on outer-ground transparency + deskew only, and claims no dark-ground/merch knockout. gemini-3-pro-image for clean legible lettering.

inputs.name: velvet_hour_listing.indd
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED asset (client-supplied, cannot be model-generated): a genuine hand-built Adobe InDesign document (.indd/.idml) for a SINGLE-RECORD A4 portrait gig-listing page - ONE artist per page. It must contain live InDesign data-merge placeholder fields <<artist_name>>, <<genre>>, <<set_date>>, <<set_time>>, <<blurb>>, and TWO @-prefixed image-path merge columns wired to two separate image frames: a poster image frame bound to @poster (so the merge drops that artist's duotone poster into the page) and a masthead image frame bound to @mark (so the merge drops the vectorised venue mark into the masthead). The venue mark rides its OWN @-image column exactly like @poster - it is NOT free-form placed at coordinates and does NOT pre-exist baked into the .indd artwork, because an agent-produced SVG cannot be hand-placed into a client template; it must arrive through the merge. Built by hand in InDesign so the merge fields and BOTH image fields actually bind. Explicitly NOT a convert_pdf_to_indd output (fields would not bind) and NOT a multi-record grid (document_merge_data_layout emits one file per row, so the template holds exactly one record's worth of fields).
inputs.realism_notes: document_merge_data_layout is [T] and REQUIRES a user-authored .indd carrying real <<fields>> plus genuine @-image-path columns, and it emits ONE FILE PER ROW - so a single-record listing page is the correct, connector-doable shape (four rows -> four pages). Two @-image columns (@poster, @mark) mean the merge resolves two prepped assets per row, mirroring the two-image-column pattern (@Portrait + @TierBadge) proven in AO-75: the agent-produced velvet_hour_mark.svg reaches the masthead ONLY as the @mark merge image (the same SVG path in every row), never by free-form placement and never baked into the template. Supplied as an input, not a chain output; a PDF-converted .indd or a multi-up grid would not bind/cannot be produced. document_merge_data_vector is the WRONG tool (text-only, cannot bind @poster or @mark).

inputs.name: velvet_hour_lineup.csv
inputs.gen_prompt: AUTHORED asset (client-supplied): a 4-row data-merge CSV, one row per artist, with text columns artist_name, genre, set_date, set_time, blurb and TWO @-prefixed image-path columns: @poster (whose cells resolve to the four duotone posters the agent produces, one per row) and @mark (whose cells all hold the SAME agent-produced velvet_hour_mark.svg path, identical in every row, so the merge drops the venue mark into each page's masthead frame). Rows: Junie Ash / indie-folk; The Paper Kestrels / alt-country; Odette Vann / jazz; Cinder & Salt / post-punk - each with a set date and time on the venue's monthly night and a one-line blurb. Header names match the <<fields>> in velvet_hour_listing.indd and the @poster / @mark columns exactly.
inputs.realism_notes: The @poster and @mark columns are the binding contract: the agent points @poster at its own produced duotone posters (one per artist) and @mark at its own produced velvet_hour_mark.svg (the SAME path in all four rows) so document_merge_data_layout places each artist's poster on that artist's page AND the venue mark in every masthead - the agent's vector mark reaches the layout through this second @-image column, not by free-form placement. Row count = 4 fixes the page=row acceptance gate. Copy binds verbatim; no rewriting.

outputs.name: VelvetHour_Sizzle.mp4
outputs.spec: A short social sizzle reel SHORTENED from the one long single-camera take by video_create_quick_cut (the AI selects the cut - an engagement-driven visual edit that shortens the single source, its duration strictly less than the multi-minute take, not a frame-accurate timeline trim and not an assembly of clips). Native audio retained. Landscape, source resolution. Supporting video deliverable for Instagram/Facebook/YouTube.

outputs.name: VelvetHour_Sizzle_vertical_9x16.mp4
outputs.spec: A same-length 9:16 vertical reframe of the sizzle reel produced by video_resize (subject-aware reframe of the existing cut, keeping the performer in shot). For stories/reels. No new footage, no re-cut - a reframe of VelvetHour_Sizzle.

outputs.name: velvet_hour_promos_neutralized_masters_x4
outputs.spec: Four RETAINED card-bearing neutralised MASTER frames (Junie Ash, The Paper Kestrels, Odette Vann, Cinder & Salt) - each the full-frame neutralised photo with its in-frame 18% grey card and white swatch STILL PRESENT, straightened where tilted, kept at camera scale (the card is NOT cropped from these). This is the artifact the grader measures neutrality on, because the card is only in frame here. Acceptance (grader-checked ON THIS master, where the card exists): every grey card reads visually neutral (R,G,B within a tight tolerance of each other), the four cards sit at ONE shared white point and brightness, no white clipped to 255 / no black crushed to 0, and Odette's card reads neutral with her amber styling intact (white balance held, not cooled). The agent REPORTS the final per-photo white-balance (temperature/tint) and exposure move it applied - an applied-settings log, not a measured readout (the agent never reads a pixel value; it neutralises by eye and reports the params it set). DELIVERABLE (the neutrality-grading master).

outputs.name: velvet_hour_promos_matched_x4
outputs.spec: Four full-colour artist promo WEB THUMBNAILS derived from the retained masters (velvet_hour_promos_neutralized_masters_x4) - the SAME matched frames with the grey card and swatch CROPPED OUT and resized for web (long edge ~2048 px, sRGB). Because the card is cropped from these files, neutrality is NOT graded here - it is graded on the retained card-bearing master above; these crops are checked only for card-EXCLUSION (no grey card or swatch left anywhere in frame), that they carry the matched look of their graded master (the four sit at one shared white point and brightness), and no white clipped to 255 / no black crushed to 0. Odette's warm styling preserved. DELIVERABLE.

outputs.name: velvet_hour_duotone_posters_x4
outputs.spec: Four single-hue duotone poster treatments of the SAME four artists - the venue's signature look: a deliberate tonal grade (desaturated to a single house hue via a monochromatic tint riding an authored contrast/black-point base) applied to the MATCHED frames so all four sit at ONE shared density - deep and moody but nothing crushed to pure black and no channel clipped. Cropped to the listing image frame at >=300 DPI at the A4 trim. These are the @poster images the merge places. Acceptance (grader-checked): consistent hue and one shared density across all four; shadow detail retained (no dead-black clip); built as a tonal grade, not a one-click preset. DELIVERABLE.

outputs.name: VelvetHour_GigNight_poster_still.jpg
outputs.spec: A gig-night poster still: one strong frame pulled from the single-camera take by video_render_frame (a 4K still), given the same signature single-hue duotone treatment as the artist posters, cropped/resized to a social poster size (honest downscale of the 4K frame, never upscaled). A designed still, not a plate. DELIVERABLE.

outputs.name: velvet_hour_mark.svg
outputs.spec: Clean vector SVG of the Velvet Hour venue mark (hand-lettered serif wordmark + moth-over-lamp glyph), traced ONLY after the scan is straightened, crisped, cropped to the mark and its OUTER paper ground knocked to transparency - razor-sharp and skew-free. Gated on outer-ground transparency + deskew ONLY: the serif wordmark's enclosed counters (the bowls of the three e's and the o) are crisped to WHITE by the knockout, NOT punched transparent, because image_remove_background isolates only the outer ground and cannot open an enclosed interior counter. The mark is therefore placed EXCLUSIVELY on the LIGHT listing-PDF masthead, where those white-filled counters read invisible against the pale masthead ground (exactly how AO-82's QUARTERLY wordmark passed) - no dark-ground or merch-scale knockout is claimed. Reaches the listing masthead ONLY through the @mark merge image column (same SVG path bound in every roster row) - never free-form placed at coordinates. DELIVERABLE.

outputs.name: VelvetHour_Lineup_Listing.pdf
outputs.spec: The printed lineup sheet: exactly four press-ready A4 portrait pages - ONE single-record page per lineup row (page-count = row-count = 4) - produced by merging velvet_hour_lineup.csv into the authored velvet_hour_listing.indd via document_merge_data_layout and exporting with document_render_layout. Each page places that artist's duotone poster through the @poster image column, drops the vector venue mark into the masthead through the SECOND @mark image column (not free-form placed), and sets <<artist_name>>/<<genre>>/<<set_date>>/<<set_time>>/<<blurb>> verbatim from the row; each placed poster renders at >=300 DPI at trim. Acceptance gate: page count == data row count == 4 (a collapsed or empty-frame merge fails this). DELIVERABLE.

Prep-before-trace step 1: the venue-mark scan sits ~2 deg rotated on the bed - straighten so the vector edges are square. Feeding the raw skewed scan to vectorize would bake in the rotation.

Prep-before-trace step 2: push contrast/clarity and drive the off-white paper toward clean white so the ink-black lettering and glyph separate hard from the ground - a soft low-contrast scan traces into ragged, doubled edges.
Prep-before-trace step 3: crop away the scan margin to the tight bounds of the mark so vectorize traces only the mark, not the paper field.

Prep-before-trace step 4: knock the OUTER off-white paper ground to transparency so the trace captures the letterforms and glyph only, not a rectangle of paper. remove_background -> transparency (NOT select->invert->fill). Note the tool isolates only the OUTER ground: the serif counters (the e/e/e bowls and the o) are enclosed interior negative space and stay crisped to WHITE, not transparent - which is fine because the mark is bound only into the LIGHT masthead where white counters are invisible; no dark-ground/merch knockout is gated.

Now trace the prepared raster (straightened, crisped, cropped, outer-ground transparent) into a clean SVG for the LIGHT listing masthead. Tracing the raw scan instead would produce a skewed, paper-bounded, fuzzy silhouette - the trap this prep chain avoids. The enclosed serif counters carry crisped-white fill (remove_background cannot open interior negative space), invisible on the pale masthead - so the mark is gated on outer-ground transparency + deskew only and used on the light masthead alone, not on any dark/merch ground. DELIVERABLE velvet_hour_mark.svg.

chaining_note: One batch upload (1) fans into four lanes that converge on a printed package. VIDEO lane: video_metadata(2) reads the single-camera take's facts (confirming it is several minutes long, longer than any cut), then video_create_quick_cut(3) SHORTENS that one long take into the sizzle reel (output duration < source, one source only - no clip assembly) and video_resize(4) reframes the sizzle same-length to 9:16; separately video_render_frame(5) pulls a 4K still that runs the POSTER-treatment sub-chain image_apply_adjustments(6, authored tonal base) -> image_apply_monochromatic_tint(7, house hue) -> image_crop_and_resize(8, gig-night poster still). ARTIST lane: four dependent per-artist chains. Junie is straightened first (auto_straighten 9) because she is tilted; each artist is then neutralised to its own in-frame grey card by image_apply_adjustments with a correction whose SIGN and dominant move differ by frame (Junie 10 warm+lift; Kestrels 15 cool+pull-down; Odette 20 HOLD WB - the trap; Cinder 25 warm+lift-with-black-hold). Each neutralised card-in frame (junie_neutral 10 / kestrels_neutral 15 / odette_neutral 20 / cinder_neutral 25) is itself RETAINED as one of the four card-bearing masters (velvet_hour_promos_neutralized_masters_x4) on which the grader measures neutrality, then forks: a crop that removes the grey card to the matched full-colour web thumbnail (11,16,21,26 -> velvet_hour_promos_matched_x4, checked only for card-exclusion + matched look) AND a poster sub-chain image_apply_adjustments(12/17/22/27, the SAME signature tonal base to one shared density) -> image_apply_monochromatic_tint(13/18/23/28, the SAME house hue) -> image_crop_and_resize(14/19/24/29 -> the four @poster images). Crucially every poster base consumes the artist's *_neutral (matched) frame, never the raw, so the four posters converge on one density. MARK lane: prep-before-trace auto_straighten(30) -> crisp adjustments(31) -> crop_to_bounds(32) -> remove_background to transparency(33) -> vectorize(34 -> velvet_hour_mark.svg). MERGE: document_merge_data_layout(35) binds the CSV into the authored .indd (one page per row), resolving BOTH image columns - @poster (each artist's duotone poster) and @mark (the shared agent-produced velvet_hour_mark.svg into the masthead, mirroring AO-75's @Portrait+@TierBadge two-image-column pattern so the agent's vector reaches the layout without free-form placement) - and document_render_layout(36) exports the four-page press PDF. Every post-upload step consumes a named prior output; the merge converges all four artist chains plus the mark and template. 36 calls, 14 distinct Adobe tools.
difficulty_rationale: Long-horizon flagship rebuilt from the killed analyze/report version: 36 connector calls, 14 distinct Adobe tools across four groups (video cut/reframe/frame-pull/metadata, image grade/tint/crop/straighten/knockout/vectorize, asset upload, document merge/export), far above the >=10 call / >=6 distinct-tool floor even after stripping the single upload and the two auto_straighten auto-ops. Difficulty is DEPTH, not repetition: the four artist neutralisations are NOT one recipe run four times - each is a per-frame WB/exposure delta whose SIGN flips by shooting session (cool Session-A frames warm up, warm Session-B frames cool down) and whose dominant move differs (WB-led on Junie/Kestrels, exposure-recovery on the dark Cinder, and a deliberate HOLD on the already-neutral Odette), so a blanket batch correction visibly fails the matched-set gate. Layered on top is an agent-AUTHORED signature look built from primitives (a desaturate/black-floor/contrast tonal base plus a single-hue monochromatic tint) that must be applied to the MATCHED frames and land all four posters at ONE shared density - duotoning the raw mismatched frames prints four different densities. Plus a genuine prep-before-trace vectorize of a skewed off-white scan, and a one-file-per-row data-merge into a hand-authored single-record template gated on page-count==row-count. Respects every hard limit: the video lane only shortens one long single-camera take (video_create_quick_cut, the AI's creative decision, output duration < the multi-minute source, no multi-clip assembly), reframes that shorter sizzle same-length (video_resize) and pulls stills (video_render_frame) - no timeline trim, no motion graphics, no compositing; image_apply_monochromatic_tint is used whole-image where a duotone SHOULD be whole-image (not a masked-recolor workaround); image_crop_and_resize is downscale-only from 4K video frames and ~4000 px stills (never upscaled/canvas-extended); knockout is remove_background to transparency (not select->invert->fill); no image_fill_area, no image_adjust_hsl rotation, no image_apply_color_overlay; convert_pdf_to_indd is NOT a merge target and document_merge_data_vector (text-only) is explicitly avoided; deprecated adjust_* tools are replaced by image_apply_adjustments. No measurement tool: the agent works to the grey card by eye and reports the parameters it applied; the grader measures the card.
hardness_rationale: FAILURE GATE (a wrong DECISION, not a self-measurement): four promos each carry an in-frame 18% grey card and the acceptance criterion is that each finished card reads visually neutral with the four matched to ONE white point and brightness - and the agent must REPORT the per-photo white-balance/exposure move it applied, so an eyeballed or uniform correction is caught. It is genuinely trippable: the correction SIGN flips by session (warm the cool frames, cool the warm frame), so one blanket move breaks the set; the dark Cinder frame needs exposure recovery while holding its black point; and a second density gate rides the duotone - if the poster base is built on the raw mismatched frames instead of the matched ones, the four posters print at four different densities and the lineup reads incoherent. HUMAN-HARD ELEMENTS (>=2): (1) cross-asset consistency to a measurable target - four differently-lit frames neutralised to one white point AND, after treatment, one shared duotone density, none crushed to pure black; (2) prep-before-trace discipline on a skewed, off-white, margin-padded venue-mark scan (straighten->crisp->crop-to-bounds->knock-to-transparency) before vectorize; (3) constraint-reasoning around tool limits - all image placement only via genuine @-image-column authored .indd merges, including the agent's OWN produced velvet_hour_mark.svg which cannot be free-form placed and cannot pre-exist in the client template, so it must ride a SECOND @-image column (@mark, same path every row) exactly like AO-75's @Portrait+@TierBadge pattern (text-only vector merge and convert_pdf_to_indd both fail to bind), knockout via remove_background not select->invert->fill, and the venue's duotone authored from primitives rather than a preset. TRAP: Odette Vann was shot under neutral light with an already-neutral grey card and is styled warm on purpose; the naive path batch-applies the 'cool the warm frames' correction (or cools an imagined orange cast), neutralising her card off-neutral and stripping the warm styling she is selling - the correct path reads THAT card and holds white balance. A second trap sits in the treatment (duotoning the raw frames) and a third in the merge (a multi-up grid or a convert_pdf_to_indd template will not bind/produce). MEASURABLE ACCEPTANCE (grader-side): every grey card neutral (R,G,B within a tight tolerance) at one white point with reported per-photo params - graded on the four RETAINED card-bearing neutralised masters (the card is in frame there), while the card-cropped web thumbnails are checked only for card-EXCLUSION so no neutrality tolerance is ever stated against a file the workflow crops the card out of; the four duotone posters at one shared hue and density with shadow detail retained (no channel clipped to 0/255); the mark a clean, skew-free vector with its OUTER paper ground knocked transparent (the enclosed serif counters crisp to white, since remove_background cannot open interior negative space - so the mark is graded only for outer-ground transparency + deskew and is placed exclusively on the LIGHT listing masthead where the white counters read invisible, exactly as AO-82's QUARTERLY wordmark passed; no dark-ground/merch knockout is claimed) placed via the @mark merge column; and exactly one press-ready >=300 DPI A4 listing page per lineup row (page-count = row-count = 4).
